BILL DETAILS
SOURCES & METHODOLOGY

A map for exploration.

The map shows 2025 bills for the 50 states and the District of Columbia. Seventeen bills are source-checked enactments, with signature dates checked against official records. The rest are bills LegiScan recorded as passed by a legislature. Those rows do not verify a governor’s signature or a chapter number. This is not a complete session inventory, and states cannot be ranked from these counts.

What is sourced?

The seventeen enactments have official source links and selective PolyViz paraphrases. The wider inventory uses the LegiScan title, description, status date, and legislature link stored from the 2025 session datasets. Source checking of the seventeen is by an AI assistant and is not independent legal review.

What still needs review?

Topic labels are keyword proposals. Specific issues are unreviewed phrase matches from a fixed list, including data centers, water use, mental health, Medicaid, and property tax. The issue search compares your words with each issue’s name and related phrases. Labeled bills come first, then bills whose title or summary uses those words. It does not decide what a bill does. Many bills match no issue, and a missing label does not mean the bill is unrelated. “Reviewed labels only” returns no bills, because nothing in this snapshot has an independent review.

How does the timeline work?

The slider includes bills dated on or before the selected month-end in 2025. For the seventeen enactments that date is the signature date. For every other bill it is the LegiScan status date. Effective dates are separate and appear on source-checked bills when available. A date here does not establish current enforceability, impact, or public support.

Coverage and geography

Congress is not on this state map. Bills already in the source-checked set are not repeated in the passed inventory. Bills can have multiple topics; map counts deduplicate bills. The map is not population-adjusted.

Source check: November 18, 2026. Boundaries: us-atlas, derived from U.S. Census boundaries. Map license.
